A body is an active entity with a RigidBody component and colliders; the functions fail for other entities. Vectors are in world space, angular values in radians. members.name: AudioPlay
members.comment: Audio (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). Sources are entities with an AudioSource component, which holds the clip, volume, pitch, looping and 3D settings. The functions fail (false, 0) while the scene plays without audio, for entities without an AudioSource component or inactive ones, and for clips that are not audio clips. AudioPlay starts the clip or resumes it (a clip that is still loading starts once it is ready); AudioPause keeps the position, AudioStop rewinds; AudioIsPlaying is also true while the start waits for the clip or the scene is paused. Positions are in seconds.

members.comment: Sounds that belong to no entity: they pause and stop with the scene. Without spatialization, or at a world position. volume >= 0 and pitch > 0 (1: the clip's own). A clip that takes longer than a quarter second to load is dropped.

members.name: AudioPlayOneShotAt
members.declaration: bool (*AudioPlayOneShotAt)(StrataScriptContext* context, StrataScriptAssetHandle clip, const float position[3], float volume, float pitch)

members.name: QuitGame
members.comment: Game flow (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). Both are requests honored once the current frame's update is done (scripts keep running until then); quitting wins over loading and later requests replace earlier ones. QuitGame ends the game with an exit code: an exported game exits with it, the editor stops play mode. LoadScene replaces the running scene with a scene asset (every entity of the current scene goes away), or restarts the running scene for the null handle; it fails for assets that are not scenes. The scene and everything it uses load in the background while the running scene goes on (GetSceneLoadProgress); it replaces the running scene once all of it is in.

members.name: ReleaseAsset
members.comment: Asset residency (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). An asset the playing scene requested with RequestAssetLoad stays loaded (pinned: never evicted to meet memory budgets) until ReleaseAsset or the end of play; requests do not add up, one release ends the scene's claim. ReleaseAsset returns false when the scene holds no request for the asset (never requested, or released already).

members.name: LoadSceneAdditive
members.comment: Scene streaming (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). LoadSceneAdditive loads a scene asset into the playing scene next to what it holds (a sub-scene) and returns the sub-scene's ID (0 when it cannot start: not a scene asset). The asset and everything it uses load in the background; then its entities are created over the following frames (a bounded number per frame), keeping the IDs they have in the asset (a sub-scene whose IDs the scene has already fails: loading one twice). UnloadSubScene removes a sub-scene: it cancels its load or destroys its entities with their descendants (at the end of the frame, like DestroyEntity); false for an unknown ID. IsSubSceneLoaded is true once every entity of the sub-scene exists.

members.name: GetSceneLoadProgress
members.comment: How far the scene LoadScene asked for has loaded, in [0, 1] (a loading bar), or -1 while no switch is under way.

members.name: GetAssetLoadProgress
members.comment: The share of the stored bytes of the asset and everything it uses (its dependency closure) that has loaded, in [0, 1]: at 1 an instance of a prefab draws complete in its first frame. The first call loads the closure and keeps it loaded while the scene plays, like RequestAssetLoad (ReleaseAsset ends it). -1 for an asset that does not exist.

members.name: InstantiateMany
members.declaration: uint32_t (*InstantiateMany)(StrataScriptContext* context, StrataScriptAssetHandle asset, uint32_t count, const float* transforms, StrataScriptEntityID parent, StrataScriptEntityID* outEntities)
members.comment: Instantiates a prefab or model `count` times, each root placed by a local transform (16 floats per instance, a column-major 4x4 matrix of a translation, rotation and scale, relative to `parent`, or the world for 0). Writes the root entities to outEntities (room for `count`) and returns how many it created: `count`, or 0 when it created none (a degenerate transform, an asset that is not loaded yet - its load starts, as for Instantiate - or a scene too full).

members.name: AnimatorPlay
members.declaration: bool (*AnimatorPlay)(StrataScriptContext* context, StrataScriptEntityID entity, StrataScriptString state)
members.comment: Animators (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). An animator is an entity with an Animator component. The functions fail (false, 0, empty) while the scene plays without animation, for entities without an Animator component, for states and parameters its controller does not have (or of another type), and for joints its skeleton does not have. Commands given while the controller still loads apply once it is loaded. AnimatorPlay jumps to a state, AnimatorCrossFade blends to it over `seconds`; AnimatorPlayClip plays an animation clip without the controller's transitions until a state is played again. A trigger stays set until a transition consumes it or AnimatorResetTrigger clears it. The speed is the Animator component's (|speed| <= 100).

members.name: CharacterMove
members.declaration: bool (*CharacterMove)(StrataScriptContext* context, StrataScriptEntityID entity, const float velocity[3])
members.comment: Character controllers (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). A controller is an active entity with an enabled CharacterController component and no RigidBody; the functions fail for other entities, for non-finite values and while the scene plays without physics. What they set takes effect at the next fixed step. CharacterMove sets the velocity (meters per second, world space) the character walks with until the next call: the horizontal part moves it along the ground, the vertical part counts only while its GravityScale is 0. CharacterJump makes it move up at `speed` meters per second at its next fixed step, on the ground or not. CharacterTeleport moves it and its entity to a world position at once (its feet: the entity's origin), keeping its walk velocity and dropping its vertical velocity. CharacterGetState reads it after its last fixed step.

members.name: IsGamepadConnected
members.comment: Gamepads (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). Gamepads are numbered 0 to 3; buttons (0 to 14) and axes (0 to 5) follow the GLFW gamepad mapping, an Xbox-style layout (the SDK's GamepadButton and GamepadAxis). Sticks range from -1 to 1 with +X right and +Y up, triggers from 0 (released) to 1; the values are the device's, without a dead zone (the SDK applies one). Like keys, buttons and axes report nothing from the device while the game has no input focus (simulated input still comes through).

members.name: SetWindowMode
members.comment: The game's window (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). Requests are checked at once and applied after the frame: a shipped game changes its window, the editor's play mode records them (editor.status, a notice in the game view) without touching the editor's window, a headless game accepts them. SetWindowMode takes a StrataScriptWindowMode; SetResolution 1 to 16384 pixels per side. GetWindowSize reports the pixels the game renders into now (the window's framebuffer, the editor's game view).

members.name: WriteSaveFile
members.declaration: bool (*WriteSaveFile)(StrataScriptContext* context, StrataScriptString name, const void* data, uint64_t size)
members.comment: Save files (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use): named byte blobs in the game's save directory (a shipped game: <user data>/<Game>/Saves; the editor: <project>/.strata/Saves). Names are 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, spaces, '-', '_' and '.' (not at the start or end), without "..": the engine refuses others, so no name reaches another directory. Writes replace the file atomically (at most 64 MiB). The calls read and write the disk before they return: keep saves small. ReadSaveFile copies at most `capacity` bytes and reports the file's size in outSize (false for a file that does not exist); ListSaveFiles copies the names, sorted and each followed by '\n', following the text buffer protocol.

members.name: PhysicsSetLayersCollide
members.declaration: bool (*PhysicsSetLayersCollide)(StrataScriptContext* context, uint32_t layerA, uint32_t layerB, bool collide)
members.comment: Collision layers (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). Bodies and character controllers are on one of the layers 0 to 31 and collide only when the playing scene's layer matrix (its copy of the project's collision layers, which the editor's Project Settings edit) lets their layers collide. PhysicsSetLayersCollide changes the playing scene's matrix (symmetric; a layer may be paired with itself); physics applies it before its next step and wakes resting bodies. It lasts while the scene plays (the next scene starts with the project's matrix again) and fails for layers outside 0 to 31. PhysicsGetLayersCollide reads the matrix (false outside the range). PhysicsGetLayerIndex finds a layer by its name (ignoring case; "Layer <index>" names a layer without a name of its own): its index, or -1 when the project has no such layer.

members.name: UIGetText
members.declaration: uint64_t (*UIGetText)(StrataScriptContext* context, StrataScriptEntityID entity, char* buffer, uint64_t capacity)
members.comment: The game UI (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). Elements are entities with UI components; each function fails (false, 0, empty text) for an entity without the component it needs: text a UIText, the image a UIImage, the color a UIImage (its tint) or else a UIText, interactable a UISelectable, the value a UISlider (clamped and snapped like input) or a UIToggle (0 or 1; switching one on switches the others of its group off). Values set here raise no OnUIValueChanged: the callbacks report the player's input. UIGetText follows the text buffer protocol; colors are display (sRGB) RGBA from 0 to 1. UISetFocus focuses an interactable selectable shown on a canvas that receives input (0 clears the focus). The pointer and the actions (StrataScriptUIAction: Submit, Cancel, Up, Down, Left, Right, the input actions of the map UI) are those of the UI's latest update, which runs before the scripts' OnUpdate.

members.name: WorldRequestCellsAround
members.declaration: uint64_t (*WorldRequestCellsAround)(StrataScriptContext* context, const float* position, float radius)
members.comment: World streaming (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use), in a scene that is a world's persistent scene (its first active World component names a World asset); in other scenes every call fails and is reported once. Positions are three floats (x, y, z), radii finite and at least 0. WorldRequestCellsAround streams the cells within the radius of the position on every enabled layer, before the sources' cells, until WorldReleaseCells or the scene stops: a request ID, 0 on failure (prefetch before a teleport or a spawn, then poll WorldIsLoadedAround). WorldIsLoadedAround tells whether every existing cell of every enabled layer within the radius is loaded. WorldSetLayerEnabled turns a layer on or off by name (a disabled layer's cells unload; false for a name the world does not have); WorldIsLayerEnabled answers 1, 0, or -1 for an unknown layer.

members.name: InputIsActionDown
members.comment: Input actions (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use): the project's named controls, which the players may rebind. An action is named "<Map>/<Action>", or by its bare name when no other map has an action of that name (ignoring case); unknown and ambiguous names fail and are reported. The state is that of the current input frame: Down, Pressed (down from this frame on) and Released (up from this frame on). InputGetActionValue writes (x, y): a Button's x is 1 while down, an Axis' x is its value (-1 to 1), a Vector2 is the vector (+Y up); zeros on failure. A disabled map's actions read as up from the next input frame, which reports the release of those held when it was disabled; InputIsActionMapEnabled answers 1, 0, or -1 for an unknown map. InputGetActionBindings copies the bindings the action uses (the players' when they replaced the project's), each followed by '\n' (the text buffer protocol); InputSetActionBindings replaces them for the players from the next input frame on, given as bindings each followed by '\n' (the last one's may be left out; empty text unbinds the action), and refuses the whole list, changing nothing, when one is no binding, one the action's kind cannot use, or there are more than 8. InputResetActionBindings restores the project's bindings of an action, or of every action for an empty name. InputSaveBindings writes the players' bindings into the game's save directory (the engine's file, outside the save files), from which the program running the game reads them when the game starts.

members.name: InputBeginBindingCapture
members.comment: Binding capture (added after InputSaveBindings, ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use), a rebinding menu's "press a control". InputBeginBindingCapture listens for the next control the player presses on the devices given (StrataScriptInputDevices bits; none, or bits it does not know, fail and are reported): a key, a mouse button, a gamepad button, or a stick or trigger pushed beyond half its range. While it listens every action reads as up, and the control captured reads as up for actions until it is let go, so the press triggers no action (and a left mouse button captured presses no UI widget; the device reads report it as any press). There is one capture: a later one (the scripts' or the editor's) replaces it. InputPollBindingCapture copies the captured binding's text (the text buffer protocol), after which the capture is over: 0 while it listens, after it was cancelled or replaced, or when none runs; a buffer too small for it gets nothing and keeps it for the next call. InputCancelBindingCapture ends the scripts' capture (false when it was not listening). Play stopping cancels it.

members.name: GraphicsGetOptionCount
members.comment: Graphics options (added after InputCancelBindingCapture, ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use): the players' choice of rendering quality, a game's options menu. The options are the fields of the project's Graphics Quality settings (the section Renderer.Quality) by name, ignoring case: "Preset" (Low, Medium, High, Ultra, Custom) first, then a row per costly setting, so options a later engine adds reach scripts without new functions. The value in effect is the project's, the player's choices over it, and over both the preset the program's command line fixes for the session (StrataRuntime --quality); renderers follow it from the next frame (a change of shadow resolution rebuilds the shadow maps once). Setting a row that follows the preset while Preset is not Custom switches it to Custom, starting from the look in effect; the players' own rows, which every preset leaves alone (AntiAliasing, MotionBlur, DepthOfField, FilmGrain, ChromaticAberration in 0.7.0; a later engine may add others), keep the preset. The player's choices last for the session: GraphicsSaveOptions writes them into the game's save directory (the engine's file, outside the save files), from which the program running the game reads them when the game starts. Options are numbered 0 to GraphicsGetOptionCount - 1 in a fixed order for the engine's run (not across engine versions: use names). GraphicsDescribeOption fills an info struct (see StrataScriptGraphicsOptionInfo); GraphicsGetOptionChoice copies the name of a Choice option's choice (the text buffer protocol; 0 for anything else). GraphicsGetOption reads the value in effect: Bool, Int, Float, or for a Choice a String with the choice's name, copied into stringBuffer (at most stringCapacity bytes) with outValue->As.String set to { stringBuffer, full size }. GraphicsSetOption takes Bool for Bool, Int for Int, Float or Int for Float, and String (a choice's name, ignoring case) for a Choice, never a number (choices are named; their order may change between engine versions, and "2048" is a name); it refuses, changing nothing, other types and values out of range. GraphicsResetOptions removes the player's choice of an option, or of every option for an empty name (Preset: the project's quality applies again). Every function fails (0, false) when the program running the game has no graphics options.

members.name: GetStepAlpha
members.comment: Interpolation (added after GraphicsSaveOptions, ABI version 1: check ST_SCRIPT_HAS_MEMBER before use). While the scene interpolates (the project's Scene.Timing Interpolation, in exported games and the editor's Play and Simulate), what the fixed steps move is drawn between its pose before the latest stepping frame's steps and its pose after them, a constant one fixed step behind the scene's clock. GetStepAlpha is the fraction of the way this frame draws, from 0 to 1 (1 while the scene does not interpolate, is paused or is stepped), final after the frame's fixed steps (OnLateUpdate; OnUpdate reads the previous frame's). GetDrawnTransform writes the entity's world transform as it is drawn this frame (its world transform when nothing interpolates it): cameras and effects that follow a moving body read it in OnLateUpdate. ResetInterpolation draws the entity and its descendants where they are until the next fixed step moves them again: call it after moving an entity far by setting its transform in OnFixedUpdate (Teleport and CharacterTeleport do it themselves). It fails only for an entity that does not exist.

members.name: OnCollisionEnter
members.comment: Contacts of the entity's physics body (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: the engine reads them only when StructSize covers them). They reach the scripts on the entities owning the two bodies (RigidBody entities, or colliders without one), after the fixed step that found the change: Enter when the bodies start touching, Exit when they part or one of them leaves the simulation. The trigger callbacks report contacts where either body is a trigger, the collision callbacks the others. Contacts begin only for scripts on active entities; every instance that got an Enter gets its Exit, also when its entity was deactivated meanwhile (deactivation ends its contacts).

members.name: OnAnimationEvent
members.comment: Events of the entity's animator (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: the engine reads it only when StructSize covers it): the playhead of the animation controller's current state passed an event, named as in the controller. Called after the animators were evaluated, in the order the events happened; the name is valid during the call.

members.name: OnUIClick
members.comment: Events of the game UI's widgets (added after the initial set of ABI version 1: the engine reads them only when StructSize covers them), from the player's input: a button clicked, a slider's or toggle's value changed (the new value; a toggle's is 0 or 1), a selectable gained or lost the focus. Each reaches the scripts on the widget's entity, then those on its event target (when it names another entity), once per instance, before the scripts' OnUpdate of the frame and in the order the inputs happened.

functions.name: SetLayersCollide
functions.declaration: static bool SetLayersCollide(uint32_t layerA, uint32_t layerB, bool collide)
functions.comment: Collision layers: RigidBody and CharacterController layers (0 to 31) collide only when the scene's copy of the project's layer matrix lets them. SetLayersCollide changes the playing scene's matrix until the next scene starts (both ways; physics applies it before its next step and wakes resting bodies) and returns false for layers outside 0 to 31. GetLayerIndex finds a layer by the name the project gives it (ignoring case; "Layer 5" for a layer without a name): its index, or -1. A mask of a layer for the queries above: 1u << layer.

functions.declaration: static bool GetLayersCollide(uint32_t layerA, uint32_t layerB)

functions.name: Find
functions.comment: The asset at a path, or a null handle if there is none.

functions.name: RequestLoad
functions.comment: Starts loading the asset in the background and keeps it loaded while the scene plays: the engine does not evict it to stay within its memory budgets until Release (or the end of play). Returns false for unknown assets.

functions.name: Release
functions.comment: Ends the scene's request for the asset (requests do not add up): the engine may unload it again when memory is needed, and loads it again when something uses it. Returns false when the scene holds no request for the asset, and with engines that predate releasing assets (they keep requested assets loaded).

functions.name: GetLoadProgress
functions.comment: How much of the asset and everything it uses (a prefab's meshes, materials and their textures; other scenes it names are not loaded) has loaded, in [0, 1]: at 1 an instance draws complete in its first frame. The first call starts loading all of it and keeps it loaded while the scene plays, like RequestLoad (Release ends that). Negative for unknown assets, and with engines that predate it.

functions.name: IsLoaded
functions.comment: Whether every entity of it exists (they appear over the frames after the load, a bounded number per frame).

functions.name: Unload
functions.comment: Removes it: stops its load, and takes its entities out of the game at once (inactive: not drawn, updated or simulated); they are destroyed with their descendants over the following frames (their scripts receive OnDestroy). Loading the same scene again meanwhile waits until they are gone. Returns false when it is gone already.

functions.name: CreateEntity
functions.declaration: static Entity CreateEntity(std::string_view name = "Entity", Entity parent = Entity())
functions.comment: Creates an empty entity (with a Transform) under `parent`, or as a root when the parent is null.

functions.name: GetEntity
functions.comment: The entity with this UUID, or a null entity if it does not exist.

functions.name: FindEntityByName
functions.comment: The first entity with this name in hierarchy order.

functions.name: FindEntitiesByTag
functions.comment: Every entity with this tag, in hierarchy order.

functions.name: GetPrimaryCamera
functions.comment: The camera the game view renders from (the first active primary camera), or a null entity.

functions.name: Instantiate
functions.declaration: static Entity Instantiate(AssetHandle asset, Entity parent = Entity())
functions.comment: Instantiates a prefab or model under `parent` (or as a root) and returns its root entity. Scripts on the new entities exist right away (GetScript works); their OnCreate runs before their first update. Never waits for loading: if the asset is not loaded yet, this starts loading it and returns a null entity. Request assets early (Assets::RequestLoad, e.g. in OnCreate) and instantiate once Assets::IsLoaded(asset) is true.

functions.name: Instantiate
functions.declaration: static Entity Instantiate(AssetHandle asset, const glm::vec3& translation, const glm::quat& rotation = glm::quat(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f), const glm::vec3& scale = glm::vec3(1.0f), Entity parent = Entity())
functions.comment: Instantiates with the given local transform for the root (relative to the parent, or the world for roots). It replaces the prefab root's whole transform: its scale is `scale` (1 unless passed), not the prefab's.

functions.name: InstantiateMany
functions.declaration: static std::vector<Entity> InstantiateMany(AssetHandle asset, const std::vector<glm::mat4>& transforms, Entity parent = Entity())
functions.comment: Instantiates a prefab or model once per transform in one call (a forest, a crowd): each instance's root gets its transform as local transform (relative to `parent`, or the world for roots; translation, rotation and scale only). Returns the roots in the order of the transforms, or none: for a degenerate transform (a zero scale), an asset that is not loaded yet (its load starts, as for Instantiate; see Assets::GetLoadProgress) or a scene that cannot hold them.

functions.name: LoadAdditive
functions.comment: Loads a scene asset into this scene next to what it holds, as a sub-scene: the asset and everything it uses load in the background, then its entities appear over the next frames (each keeps the ID it has in the asset, so loading a sub-scene twice fails: unload it first). Their scripts get OnCreate like any new entity's. Returns a null sub-scene for assets that are not scenes, and with engines that predate it.

functions.name: GetEntity
functions.comment: The entity this script is attached to.

functions.name: GetDeltaTime
functions.comment: Duration of the current frame in seconds (scaled by the time scale).

functions.name: GetFixedDeltaTime
functions.comment: Duration of one fixed update step in seconds.

functions.name: GetElapsedTime
functions.comment: Seconds of simulation since the scene started playing.

functions.name: GetFrameIndex
functions.comment: Number of completed frames since the scene started playing.

functions.name: GetTimeScale
functions.comment: Speed of the simulation (1 = real time, 0 = frozen).

functions.name: GetUnscaledDeltaTime
functions.comment: Duration of the current frame in seconds before the time scale: what menus, fades and pause screens animate with, since it goes on at time scale 0.

functions.name: GetRealTime
functions.comment: Seconds since the scene started playing, unaffected by the time scale (the sum of GetUnscaledDeltaTime).

functions.name: GetStepAlpha
functions.comment: How far between the poses before and after the latest fixed steps this frame draws what they moved (0 to 1; 1 while nothing interpolates). Final in OnLateUpdate.

functions.name: GetText
functions.comment: The text of its UIText.

functions.name: SetText
functions.comment: Sets the text of its UIText (setting the same text again costs nothing, so a HUD may set its texts every frame).

functions.name: GetImage
functions.comment: The texture of its UIImage (the null asset: the image's color alone).

functions.name: SetImage
functions.comment: Shows a texture in its UIImage (the null asset: the color alone); other assets than textures are refused.

functions.name: GetColor
functions.comment: The color of its UIImage (its tint), else of its UIText: display (sRGB) RGBA from 0 to 1.

functions.name: SetColor
functions.comment: Sets the color of its UIImage, else of its UIText (clamped to 0 to 1; non-finite colors are refused).

functions.name: IsInteractable
functions.comment: Whether its UISelectable takes input (a disabled one shows its disabled state and never gets the focus).

functions.name: GetValue
functions.comment: The value of its UISlider, or 1 for a UIToggle that is on and 0 for one that is off.

functions.name: SetValue
functions.comment: Sets the value of its UISlider (clamped to its range, rounded with WholeNumbers), or switches its UIToggle on (any value but 0; the others of its group switch off) or off.

functions.name: Focus
functions.comment: Gives its UISelectable the keyboard and gamepad focus (it must be interactable and shown on a canvas that takes input).

functions.name: GetFocused
functions.comment: The selectable with the keyboard and gamepad focus (an invalid entity without one).

functions.name: IsPointerOverUI
functions.comment: Whether the pointer is over the UI: gameplay that aims or shoots with the mouse ignores it then (the UI already hides its clicks from Input).

functions.name: IsActionPressed
functions.comment: Whether an action was pressed this frame (Cancel closes a menu: the UI raises no event for it).

functions.name: Release
functions.comment: Lets the cells go: they unload once no source wants them. False for a request the engine does not hold (refused, released already, or made in a scene that stopped).

functions.name: RequestCellsAround
functions.declaration: static WorldCellRequest RequestCellsAround(const glm::vec3& position, float radius)
functions.comment: Streams the cells within `radius` of `position` on every enabled layer (radius 0: the cells at the position).

functions.name: IsLoadedAround
functions.declaration: static bool IsLoadedAround(const glm::vec3& position, float radius)
functions.comment: Whether every existing cell of every enabled layer within `radius` of `position` is loaded.

functions.name: SetLayerEnabled
functions.declaration: static bool SetLayerEnabled(std::string_view layer, bool enabled)
functions.comment: Turns a layer of the world on or off by its name: a disabled layer's cells unload, and it streams again once enabled. Layers start as the world defines them (EnabledByDefault). False for a name the world does not have.

functions.name: IsLayerEnabled
functions.comment: Whether a layer streams; nullopt for a name the world does not have (or a scene that streams no world).

macros.name: ST_SCRIPT_CLASS
macros.comment: Registers a script class and declares its fields. Use once per class, in a .cpp file: ST_SCRIPT_CLASS(Player) { ST_SCRIPT_FIELD(Speed); ST_SCRIPT_FIELD(Target); } The class name used by Script components is the spelled type name ("Player", or "Game::Player" for ST_SCRIPT_CLASS(Game::Player)). A class without fields is registered with an empty body: ST_SCRIPT_CLASS(Spinner) {}

macros.name: ST_SCRIPT_FIELD
macros.comment: Declares a public data member of the class as a field: shown in the editor, serialized with the scene and kept across hot reloads. Supported types: bool, int32_t, float, glm::vec2/3/4, glm::quat, std::string, Strata::Entity, Strata::AssetHandle.
